reasoning: The team is at percentile 0.6983, far above the target 0.2 (top 20%). The best CV score (0.8395) is higher than the leaderboard score (0.7679) by ~0.07, indicating over‑fitting to the validation folds. No CV gain was observed in iterations 2 and 3 despite changing model focus and tuning, and the CV score has plateaued at 0.8395. The current feature set relies mainly on raw numeric/categorical columns; the planned richer feature engineering (titles, deck, ticket prefix, group size, log‑Fare, missing‑Age indicator) has not yet been applied. With only one iteration left and two submissions remaining, the most impactful next step is to apply the detailed feature plan, then retrain the LightGBM model with slightly stronger regularisation to close the CV‑LB gap and push the leaderboard score upward.
diagnosis: Score is limited by over‑fitting (CV > LB) and insufficient feature engineering. The model hyper‑parameters are already reasonable but could use more regularisation. No new predictive signals have been added beyond the baseline features, so the model cannot break out of the current performance plateau.
suggestions: Implement regex extraction: Title from Name, CabinDeck from Cabin, TicketPrefix from Ticket.
Create group‑size feature for Ticket (number of rows sharing the same Ticket).
Log‑transform Fare and add the transformed column.
Add a missing‑indicator column for Age (and any other column with missing values).
Frequency‑encode categorical columns: Ticket, Cabin, Embarked, Sex, Pclass.
Drop raw high‑cardinality text columns: Name, Ticket, Cabin, and identifier PassengerId.

Retrain the LightGBM model using the same base params but increase regularisation (e.g., min_child_samples 40, subsample 0.7, colsample_bytree 0.7, learning_rate 0.05, n_estimators 1000 with early stopping).
Validate that CV standard error is low and that the CV lower confidence bound (LCB) is close to the LB score before submitting.
Submit the new model; if budget permits, use the second remaining submission to try a slight variation (e.g., different random seed or a small change in num_leaves).
